chapter_theme: The unripe (அபக்குவன்): the unready choose blind teachers and fall with them, look outward, do not wake to the light or answer the Lord's call, say one thing and do another; the king should drive out the great sinners; and the unworthy disciple, who neither removes his impurities nor fears birth, is not to be given the teaching.
structure_note: The unripe seeker (1680 to 1683), the king's duty against sinners (1684), austerity, the Lord's nature and waking (1685 to 1687), and the unworthy disciple (1688, 1689).

1680.reading: They will not take the guru who removes blindness but take one who does not; blind and blind, playing a blind game, both fall into the pit.
1680.nuance: குருடு (blindness) is ignorance, and the repetition of குரு and குருடு makes the line a pun. The blind leading the blind into a pit is a widespread image, known also from the Upanishads and the Gospels.

1681.reading: A magic mirror has arisen in the mind, yet they do not see even its reflection in their thought; they will not polish it so the fruit of deeds departs, but go off desiring what lies outside.
1681.nuance: The mirror in the mind is read as the inner faculty in which the Lord or the self could be seen if it were cleaned; விளக்கியும் (polishing) supports this. புறக்கடை (the outer gate or back door) is taken as the outward world of the senses.

1682.reading: When called they do not answer 'what is it?'; those among kin do not know the mother's breast that flows sweet when the mouth is put to it; the formless one is the one who keeps the body.
1682.nuance: பிரசைகள் may be people, subjects or children; the verse seems to say the unripe do not answer the Lord's call nor know him as a mother's breast that gives without asking. உருவிலி (the formless one) is the Lord; ஊன்நிலை செய்யும் may mean he sustains the body. The line connections are my guess.

1683.reading: Saying one thing with the mouth and thinking another in the mind, don't do yet a third, great one; I will know you here as you are, and once I have known you, others will not take me for a madman.
1683.nuance: The first two lines are a plain demand that word, thought and deed agree. The last two are obscure: பேய் may mean a madman or a ghost, and who speaks to whom is unclear; it may be the teacher sizing up a would-be disciple.

1684.reading: If the king of the faithful does not inflict hard punishment on these sinners of the five betrayals so that they fear, and drive them off this earth, the whole earth will fall into famine and lie waste.
1684.nuance: பஞ்சத் துரோகம் is traditionally taken as the five great sins (killing, theft, liquor, adultery, and wronging the guru, in one list). அஞ்சச் சமயத்தோர் வேந்தன் may be 'the king, so that those of the sects fear' or 'the king of the faith'. பஞ்சம் (famine) puns with பஞ்ச (five).

1685.reading: The karma that those who stand in austerity undergo rests in Siva, and even the gods do not know it; for all who stand in austerity without knowing this, it is suffering that stays in births.
1685.nuance: The sense may be that the ascetic who knows offers his deeds to Siva and is freed, while austerity without that knowledge only adds to births. பவத்திடை நின்றதோர் பாடு (suffering that stands in birth) is my reading.

1686.reading: Burning with anger, scheming, doing deeds, eating, relishing, doing harm, falling back, putting oneself forward and boasting of greatness: these are not the nature of one near the Lord.
1686.nuance: இறைபால் இயற்கை அல்லவே can mean 'not the nature of the Lord' or 'not the nature of those who are with the Lord'. Placed in this chapter, the list reads as the marks of the unripe; the first reading would make it a statement about the Lord's own freedom from these.

1687.reading: They do not know the dawning and cannot see the open space; even when it dawns they will not open their eyes in it; bind fast the strong inner eyelid and see: that is the lamp that guards against the night not ending.
1687.nuance: விடிவு (dawn) and வெளி (open space) are traditionally read as the dawning of knowledge and the inner space seen in yoga. உண்ணிமை (inner eyelid) is obscure; it may mean closing the outer eyes to see within.

1688.reading: One who keeps to the path that changes the soul's set bonds, then, released from bondage, wavers, and does not think his way through the tattvas to reach the goal: to such a deluded disciple the teaching is not to be given.
1688.nuance: பெத்த மற முத்தனாகிப் பிறழ்வுற்று is hard: it may describe one who seems freed but slips back. The verse ends without naming what is not to be given; the teaching or initiation is implied.

1689.reading: He who does not know the way to remove the five abiding impurities, does not give up dipping into lust and the rest, a tangled liar who does not fear birth and death, is an outsider: he is the unworthy disciple.
1689.nuance: மலம் ஐந்து, five impurities, extends the usual three (ஆணவம், கன்மம், மாயை); tradition adds மாயேயம் and திரோதாயி. அசற்சீடன் (the unreal or unworthy disciple) is set against சற்சீடன் of the next chapter.

links.note: 1680 shows the unripe choosing a teacher who cannot remove blindness and falling with him; 1693 gives the remedy: if you take a guru, take a good one, and give him body, life and goods.
Both condemn the split between word and deed: the Kural calls the bond with such people bitter even in a dream, Tirumular warns against saying one thing, thinking another and doing a third.
Both make the king's harsh punishment of the wicked a protection of the land: the Kural likens it to weeding the young crop, Tirumular says without it the earth falls to famine.
Both tie the land's famine to tolerating the wrong people: in 1656 the ignorant who wear the garb, in 1684 the sinners the king fails to drive out.

1681 says a magic mirror has arisen in the mind (மனத்தில் எழுந்ததோர் மாயக்கண்ணாடி) but the unripe do not polish it and go after outer things. 2109 says for those who stand within the mirror and know (ஆடியுளே நின்று அறிவு செய்வார்கட்கு) the Lord becomes like a cow in milk. The inner mirror is ignored in 1681 and used in 2109, showing what the unripe miss.

Kural 262 says tapas comes to those who have it, and for others taking it up is futile (அவம்). 1685 says all who stand in tapas without knowing that its karma rests in Siva gain only suffering in births (பவத்திடை நின்றதோர் பாடு). Both say tapas taken up without its inner ground is wasted; Tirumular names that ground as knowing Siva.

1687 says the unripe do not know the dawning (விடிவதறியார) and even when it dawns will not open their eyes. 2001 says the darkness of bond and ignorance vanished as dense darkness leaves at dawn (அருணோதயம் துன்றிருள் நீங்குதல் போல). Dawn is the coming of knowledge in both; 2001 tells it happening, 1687 tells of those who sleep through it.

1688 says that to a deluded disciple who wavers and does not think through the tattvas the teaching is not to be given (பித்தான சீடனுக்கு ஈயப் பெறாதான்). Kural 720 says speaking before those not of one's own kind is nectar spilled in a dirty yard (அங்கணத்துள் உக்க அமிழ்து). The same rule, that teaching is wasted on the unfit hearer, holds for the assembly and for initiation.

1689 calls the unworthy disciple one who does not fear birth and death (பிறப்பிறப் பஞ்சாதான்) and will not leave lust. 1696 calls the true disciple one who fears the binding round of births (ஆர்த்த பிறவியின் அஞ்சி) and keeps to dharma. The two chapters define the unripe and the ripe disciple by the same test, fear of birth, stated negatively and positively.
